A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CoPeDiT for brain missing-modality and cardiac missing-slice synthesis. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original MRI synthesis comparisons, component ablations, prompt-corruption experiments, and downstream tumor-segmentation results, including supplementary material.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, multi-seed experiments, unseen-combination tests, computational measurements, and diagnostic analyses.

M1.justification: The CoPeVAE pretext tasks, prompt construction, alternating MDiT3D blocks, targeted prompt injection, and diffusion objective remain unchanged. v3 explains task-specific variants and conditioning more explicitly, but these procedures already appear in v1's methodology, architecture figures, ablations, and appendix.

E1.justification: The same brain and cardiac datasets are used. Downstream BraTS segmentation coverage expands from three real modalities plus one synthesized modality to one real modality plus three synthesized modalities (v3 Appendix C.8/Table 21), adding a more severely incomplete input scenario within the existing task.

E2.justification: The primary synthesis comparisons expand from six to nine baselines by adding DiffM4RI, APT, and ASLDM (v3 Tables 1–3). These methods also enter the retained single-synthetic-modality segmentation comparison (v3 Table 7 versus v1 Table 12). APT was cited in v1 but was not evaluated there.

E3.justification: v3 adds MAE and FVD, lesion-restricted metrics, frozen nnU-Net anatomical evaluation with Dice/HD95, and pretext-task accuracy/macro-F1. New protocols exclude specified modality combinations from both training stages and standardize inference-cost measurements. The cardiac tokenizer's training-step table changes from 200k to 100k, resolving disagreement with v1's existing 100k prose; this does not establish that training was rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's existing component, injection-position, backbone, and prompt-corruption analyses, v3 adds position-prompt replacement with mask codes, structured prompt interventions, unseen-combination robustness, lesion/anatomical fidelity, computational-cost analysis, perception accuracy, and synthesis errors grouped by prediction correctness. Figures 13–14 also introduce explicit failure analyses linking incorrect completeness predictions to degraded synthesis.

E5.justification: v1 includes ± values without an explicit multi-seed analysis. v3 Appendix C.2/Table 15 reports means and standard deviations across three independent seeds for CoPeDiT, M2DN, and ASLDM on two challenging brain settings. Figure 13 adds subgroup sample counts and dispersion. Conversely, the primary comparison tables remove the FID ± values reported in v1.

E6.justification: All 168 retained primary PSNR/SSIM/FID point estimates match, and the original segmentation results remain. v3 adds extensive baseline, metric, robustness, diagnostic, and computational results. Its new three-synthetic-modality segmentation experiment reports 87.70% average Dice for CoPeDiT, while APT slightly leads tumor-core Dice, 87.64% versus 87.49% (Table 21). These are new-setting results, not changes to v1's retained 90.23% single-synthetic-modality average. The original corruption-study SSIM/FID curves are omitted.

T1.justification: The sample partition, classification and contrastive losses, combined tokenizer loss, and diffusion objective in Equations 1–5 are mathematically unchanged. The x-prediction/x0-prediction terminology change is equivalent. Neither version supplies additional theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: v1 presents a general-purpose unified model for arbitrary incomplete scenarios and emphasizes a novel diffusion-transformer paradigm and demonstrated clinical applicability. v3 explicitly defines unification as a shared framework with task-specific models, positions MDiT3D as a tailored DiT conditioning interface, and qualifies clinical deployment as potential. These materially narrow the central scope and novelty claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive limitations concerning fixed modality vocabularies, compression-related detail loss, and hallucinated anatomy. Appendix D explicitly states that scanner, institution, protocol, and population shifts were not evaluated. It also explains how prompts complement available latents, while Appendix C.7 links completeness-prediction errors to contrast drift, modality bias, and blurred structures.

D1.justification: v3 adds CoPeVAE parameter/FLOP and wall-clock training costs, inference latency/VRAM, and measurement conditions in Section 4.5. It reconciles cardiac training details, including the main-text batch size with the value 64 already present in v1's appendix. Most architecture specifications, preprocessing, optimization settings, sampling details, and the code-access statement remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 expands to broader medical image generation, reconstruction, and completion, incorporating works such as Text2CT, MAISI-v2, and DiffuX2CT alongside newer MRI methods. The introduction also explicitly repositions MDiT3D as an adaptation of DiT rather than a fundamentally new paradigm, substantially revising the novelty framing.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, method explanations, and conclusion undergo substantial rewriting. Existing segmentation and prompt-sensitivity material moves into the main text, while injection-position and backbone ablations move to Appendix C.4. The experimental narrative is reorganized, prompt-token terminology is standardized, and dedicated limitations and discussion sections are added.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column layout to a single-column journal format. The combined brain-results table is split, tables gain metric columns and comparator rows, and qualitative panels expand with error maps and additional examples. The motivation figure is redesigned, existing t-SNE and attention displays are merged, and new intervention, accuracy, failure-case, and segmentation figures are introduced.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens support for the unchanged method through additional competitive baselines, explicit three-seed checks, held-out-combination tests, lesion-level validation, and observed failure analyses. These address gaps behind v1's broad reliability and applicability claims. Clearer definitions of unification and explicit domain-shift limitations also improve claim accuracy. Removing primary-table FID uncertainty is a reporting loss, and seed coverage remains limited, but the stronger validation and better-qualified conclusions provide a substantial net improvement.
